Graduate Programs in Molecular and Cell Biology
At a Glance
Degrees: Master of Science (MS) or PhD
Format: In person, Waltham/Boston area
Master's Program Length: MS: 1 year (part-time option available), 6 courses
Admissions Deadlines: MS: (fall) March 1, April 15, then rolling until May 15 or until cohort is full; (spring) Oct. 15 (priority), Nov. 15 (final); PhD: Dec. 1
Funding: The majority of our master’s students receive some form of scholarship. Funding for PhD students includes a competitive fellowship, a full-tuition scholarship, and health insurance benefits for five years.
School: Brandeis School of Science, Engineering and Technology
Learn More
Loading...
How do organisms function at the molecular and cellular levels? The goal of Brandeis University's Molecular and Cell Biology graduate program is to train aspiring scientists interested in solving this fundamental question. Students acquire a broad knowledge about current developments in molecular and cell biology, learn to be effective scientific communicators, and are trained to perform independent scientific research. Research areas include genetics, molecular biology, developmental biology, cell biology, and neurobiology.
Molecular and Cell Biology Degree Options
Master of Science (MS) in Molecular and Cell Biology
PhD in Molecular and Cell Biology
Both have the option of a specialization in Quantitative Biology.
Molecular and Cell Biology Curriculum
The MS program is designed to guide each student toward realizing their potential as an independent research biologist. Students are encouraged to become experts in their chosen area of research while gaining breadth in other areas represented in the program. All students gain experience conducting independent research, building on existing skills or developing new ones through project lab courses. Research areas include genetics, molecular biology, developmental biology, cell biology, structural biology, immunology, and neurobiology.
In the PhD program, flexible course requirements allow students to focus on their research interests while gaining training in cutting-edge methods and quantitative data analysis. Students strengthen their communication skills through weekly journal clubs, colloquia, and research seminars. Annual "Pizza Talks" provide opportunities to receive feedback on dissertation research from the Molecular and Cell Biology and Neuroscience community. In addition to their thesis advisor, each student's progress is guided by a three-member thesis committee, helping them build a strong network of mentors.
Molecular and Cell Biology Courses
Molecular and Cell Biology Career Paths and Outcomes
Graduates of the MS program have pursued careers in biotechnology, medical research, academic research, medicine, policy, and patent law.
PhD graduates have gone on to careers in academia, industry, and government, while others have chosen teaching positions at colleges and high schools or applied their scientific training to careers in science policy, publishing, and law.

Cost and Funding
Master's Students
The majority of our master’s students will receive some form of scholarship. Brandeis offers several merit and need-based scholarships. Enrolled students may be offered paid course assistantships in some programs.
Doctoral Students
Funding includes a competitive fellowship, a full-tuition scholarship, and health insurance benefits for five years.
